mechanism: Six provided edge/gradient layers (magnetic tilt/tc, isostatic gravity anomaly, TMI, detrended elevation, conductivity, geodetic strain invariant) are robust-normalised; for each, a multiscale (sigma=1,2,4 px) Gaussian-derivative edge magnitude is multiplied by cross-scale orientation coherence to isolate through-going linear discontinuities. Rank-normalised layers are combined by GEOMETRIC MEAN (requiring agreement across independent physics) and mildly weighted by depth to conductive base. From this catalogue-independent surface, TWO populations of non-maximum-suppressed peaks are emitted as confidence-1 dots, both using fold-local VISIBLE-fault geometry only: (1) near-catalogue continuation dots within a 2-8 px halo (physics-ranked) and (2) off-catalogue whole-footprint lineament dots. Mapped-fault pixels are excluded by a 2 px collar. Emission hedges the hide-and-recover proxy's near-fault bias while keeping coverage of genuinely-new off-catalogue faults that the leaderboard rewards.
named_non_fault_mimic: Aeromagnetic flight-line leveling artifacts and buried intrusive/dike or lithologic contacts — coherent multiscale linear edges in potential fields that are not through-going brittle faults. Mitigation: cross-physics geometric mean; caveat: a deeply buried intrusive contact can remain indistinguishable from a blind fault.
